prospects.message:
Hi Critical Thinking team,

Your episode on browser logic errors and XS-Leaks with Jorian Woltjer caught my attention while researching a guest fit.

I’m Ruth, helping Rafay Baloch with outreach for Web Hacking Arsenal: A Practical Guide to Modern Web Pentesting. He is open to a technical conversation about browser security and web application testing.

A possible angle: how researchers turn an unexpected browser behavior into a testable hypothesis, and what that teaches bug bounty hunters about finding gaps in their approach. I’d coordinate concrete examples with Rafay before recording.

Would a short guest outline on that angle be useful?

Best,
Ruth Maclang
Outreach for Rafay Baloch

prospects.angle: A short, practical session about turning findings into reusable tests
prospects.subject: Proposed lightning talk: one web finding, better testing questions
prospects.message:
Proposed title: One web finding, better testing questions
Format: 10–15 minute lightning talk
Speaker: Rafay Baloch

Proposed abstract:
Finding a vulnerability is one step; understanding what else it implies is another. This session would explore how to move from a single web application finding to a small set of useful follow-on tests in an authorized environment. It would show how to separate observations from assumptions, document a reproducible case, and turn the result into a lesson developers can use.

Intended audience: web application testers, bug bounty practitioners and AppSec engineers.

Takeaways: a clearer testing hypothesis, a stronger evidence trail and a reusable regression question.

Coordinator: Ruth Maclang. Rafay’s final abstract, example and availability will be confirmed before submission.

Book reference: https://www.routledge.com/Web-Hacking-Arsenal-A-Practical-Guide-to-Modern-Web-Pentesting/Baloch/p/book/9781032447193
prospects.needs: Obtain Rafay’s approved abstract, speaker bio, recording agreement and London/remote availability before submission. Keep book promotion out of the talk; book may appear in the speaker bio. No travel commitment.
prospects.followUp: Follow the submission process. Record any acknowledgement before setting a follow-up; avoid duplicate form submissions.

prospects.angle: Browser trust boundaries explained for working software engineers
prospects.subject: Topic proposal: browser trust boundaries for web engineers
prospects.message:
Hi Robert,

I’m Ruth, coordinating outreach for Rafay Baloch, author of Web Hacking Arsenal. Following your topic-proposal format, I’d like to propose a discussion of browser trust boundaries for web engineers:

• How browser security assumptions influence application design.
• Where developers should distinguish client behavior from server-enforced controls.
• How to turn an observed browser behavior into a testable security question.
• What evidence makes a finding reproducible and useful to developers.
• How to carry that learning into regression testing.

Rafay is open to a practical, vendor-neutral discussion. Supporting work: Web Hacking Arsenal, published by CRC Press, and its public companion repository. We would agree concrete examples with him before recording.

Would this topic be worth developing for the show?

Best,
Ruth Maclang
Outreach for Rafay Baloch
